ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the brain is at the upper part, the spinal cord is at the lower left, and the muscle is on the right; two structures, a and b, are marked inside the muscle. a is located inside the muscle, with a neural pathway above it connected to neuron numbered ①, and the pathway direction is shown as transmitting information inside the muscle to the spinal cord; at the same time, the figure also has efferent connections from central or spinal neurons acting on a. b is also located inside the muscle and is connected with the central efferent pathway, and can undergo contraction. Reasoning: In a reflex arc, the structure that can receive a stimulus and transmit excitation into the nerve center through an afferent nerve is the receptor; the structure that can receive efferent nerve innervation and produce a response, such as muscle contraction, is the effector. In the figure, a has afferent connections, indicating that it can sense the muscle state and transmit information to the center; it also receives efferent innervation, indicating that it can also serve as a structure producing a response. Therefore, in the reflex arc, a has both the functions of a receptor and an effector.
